status: One integrated source-fit structural understanding programme, not a rollup of linked child codes or learner attainment.

member.task: Choose the beam as member; explain external load/support, upper compression/lower tension ONLY for the supplied sagging support case, and why rest does not mean absent internal force.

outside.task: Translate the actual given column load/support into a force diagram and identify the resulting squeezing/deformation. Distinguish forces on this body from forces it exerts.

built-resistance.task: Explain how the stated roof connection withstands the supplied uplift and why a window barrier addresses a different debris-impact route; both have limits.

natural-resistance.task: Explain how the actual buttress support helps the tree withstand a specified tipping load; contrast with a breathing-root feature that serves another function.

protective-design.task: Explain why the helmet’s supplied protective layer can reduce harmful loading consequences, with its deformation/replacement/activity-fit limit; do not certify a real helmet.

actions: Actually complete all five linked prepared cases, retaining their original given conditions, source evidence and limits. In one portfolio explain loading→internal/material/structural response→resistance/protection for both natural and built structures.

Compare the beam’s rest/deformation, roof connection and rooted tree: relate outside loading to what changes or resists inside/at the support, distinguishing no motion from no force. Explain why changing supports, material or the kind of load can change the outcome.

Use a changed original brief: an unverified support arrangement and a proposed feature whose known role is gas exchange rather than support. State which force relationships can be reasoned from supplied facts and which cannot, rather than apply a memorised top/bottom rule or call every feature protective.
Explain why no one method guarantees survival under every load and why a designed protective object and an organism’s physical trait can both affect consequences without serving identical purposes.

wholeClaimBoundary: The actual overall duty asks force/structural-resistance understanding. This portfolio directly tests integrated relationships; it does not certify every whole contributor from one child example.
Each linked report retains full-claim readiness and actual source/fixture limits. Existing quantitative topics, all old whole claims and all child-code judgments remain unchanged.
Original physical models and given accounts are not performed experiments or measured building/organism capacities. Actual delivery evidence is separate from authoring coverage.
consumerBoundary: Five existing-topic overall component pairs, no new claim/guide/context/age/dependency or learner write.
